'''Maria Chudnovsky''' (born January 6, 1977) is an [[Israel]]i-[[United States|American]] mathematician working on [[graph theory]] and [[combinatorial optimization]].<ref name=CV>{{cite web|title=Maria Chudnovsky Curriculum Vitae|url=https://web.math.princeton.edu/~mchudnov/cv.pdf|publisher=Princeton University|access-date=21 Jan 2024}}</ref>  She is a [[MacArthur Fellows Program|2012 MacArthur Fellow]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2012 MacArthur Foundation 'Genius Grant' Winners|url=http://bigstory.ap.org/article/2012-macarthur-foundation-genius-grant-winners#overlay-context=users/rjagodzinski|work=1 October 2012|publisher=Associated Press|access-date=1 October 2012|archive-date=2 October 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121002000603/http://bigstory.ap.org/article/2012-macarthur-foundation-genius-grant-winners#overlay-context=users/rjagodzinski|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Chudnovsky is a professor in the department of mathematics at [[Princeton University]]. She grew up in [[Russia]] (attended [[Saint Petersburg Lyceum 30]]) and [[Israel]], studying at the [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology|Technion]],<ref name="clay"/> and received her Ph.D. in 2003 from [[Princeton University]] under the supervision of [[Paul Seymour (mathematician)|Paul Seymour]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|name=Maria Chudnovsky|id=69866}}</ref> After postdoctoral research at the [[Clay Mathematics Institute]],<ref name="clay">{{citation|url=http://www.claymath.org/library/annual_report/ar2005/05report_chud.pdf|title=Interview with Research Fellow Maria Chudnovsky|publisher=[[Clay Mathematics Institute]]|year=2005}}.</ref> she became an assistant professor at Princeton University in 2005, and moved to [[Columbia University]] in 2006. By 2014, she was the Liu Family Professor of Industrial Engineering and Operations Research at Columbia. She returned to Princeton as a professor of mathematics in 2015.<ref name=CV/>

Chudnovsky is an editor for a number of mathematical journals, including ''[[Combinatorica]]'', ''[[Journal of Combinatorial Theory|Journal of Combinatorial Theory Series B]]'', ''[[Journal of Graph Theory]]'' and ''[[Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society]]''.{{r|CV}}

==Research==
{{external media | width = 210px | float = right  | headerimage =
 | video1 = [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ooI7Jimh0M0 Mathematician Maria Chudnovsky: 2012 MacArthur Fellow], [[MacArthur Foundation]]<ref name="macf">{{cite web | title =Maria Chudnovsky | work =[[MacArthur Fellows Program]] | publisher =[[MacArthur Foundation]] | date =October 2, 2012 | url =http://www.macfound.org/fellows/862/ | access-date =December 13, 2014 }}</ref> }}

Chudnovsky's contributions to [[graph theory]] include the proof of the [[strong perfect graph theorem]] (with [[Neil Robertson (mathematician)|Neil Robertson]], [[Paul Seymour (mathematician)|Paul Seymour]], and [[Robin Thomas (mathematician)|Robin Thomas]]) characterizing [[perfect graph]]s as being exactly the graphs with no odd [[induced subgraph|induced]] [[cycle (graph theory)|cycles]] of length at least 5 or their [[complement graph|complements]].<ref>{{citation| last = Mackenzie | first = Dana| date = July 5, 2002| doi = 10.1126/science.297.5578.38| issue = 5578| journal = [[Science (journal)|Science]]| page = 38| pmid = 12098683| title = Mathematics: Graph theory uncovers the roots of perfection| volume = 297| s2cid = 116891342}}.</ref><ref>{{citation| last = Cornuéjols| first = Gérard| author-link = Gérard Cornuéjols| contribution = The strong perfect graph conjecture| location = Beijing| mr = 1957560| pages = 547–559| publisher = Higher Ed. Press| title = Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, Vol. III (Beijing, 2002)| url = http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM2002.3/Main/icm2002.3.0547.0560.ocr.pdf| year = 2002| access-date = 2012-08-11| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140407094629/http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM2002.3/Main/icm2002.3.0547.0560.ocr.pdf| archive-date = 2014-04-07| url-status = dead}}</ref><ref>{{citation| last1 = Roussel | first1 = Florian| last2 = Rusu | first2 = Irena| last3 = Thuillier | first3 = Henri| doi = 10.1016/j.disc.2009.05.024| issue = 20| journal = [[Discrete Mathematics (journal)|Discrete Mathematics]]| mr = 2552645| pages = 6092–6113| title = The strong perfect graph conjecture: 40 years of attempts, and its resolution| volume = 309| year = 2009| s2cid = 16049392| doi-access = free| citeseerx = 10.1.1.230.1328}}.</ref> Other research contributions of Chudnovsky include co-authorship of the first [[polynomial time|polynomial-time]] algorithm for recognizing perfect graphs (time bounded by a polynomial of degree 9),{{sfnp|Chudnovsky|Cornuéjols|Liu|Seymour|2005}} a structural characterization of the [[claw-free graph]]s,{{sfnp|Chudnovsky|Seymour|2005}} and progress on the [[Erdős–Hajnal conjecture]].<ref name="Chudnovsky Scott Seymour Spirkl 2023 pp. 997–1014">{{cite journal | last1=Chudnovsky | first1=Maria | last2=Scott | first2=Alex | last3=Seymour | first3=Paul | last4=Spirkl | first4=Sophie | title=Erdős–Hajnal for graphs with no 5-hole | journal=Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society | publisher=Wiley | volume=126 | issue=3 | date=2023-01-31 | issn=0024-6115 | doi=10.1112/plms.12504 | pages=997–1014| doi-access=free | arxiv=2102.04994 }}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
In 2004 Chudnovsky was named one of the "Brilliant 10" by [[Popular Science|Popular Science magazine]].<ref>{{citation|title=Maria Chudnovsky|url=https://www.popsci.com/scitech/article/2004-06/maria-chudnovsky|journal=Popular Science|last=Minkel|first=J. R.|date=June 29, 2004}}</ref> Her work on the strong perfect graph theorem won for her and her co-authors the 2009 [[Fulkerson Prize]].<ref>{{citation
 | date = December 2011
 | journal = [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]
 | pages = 1475–1476
 | title = 2009 Fulkerson Prizes
 | url = https://www.ams.org/notices/201011/rtx101101475p.pdf}}.</ref>
In 2012 she was awarded a "genius award" under the [[MacArthur Fellows Program]].<ref>{{citation|newspaper=[[New York Times]]|url = https://www.nytimes.com/2012/10/02/arts/macarthur-fellows-named-for-2012.html|title=Surprise Grants Transforming 23 More Lives|date=October 1, 2012|first=Felicia R.|last=Lee}}</ref><ref>[http://www.macfound.org/fellows/862/ Maria Chudnovsky], MacArthur Foundation, October 2, 2012.</ref> She  was elected as a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in the 2024 class of fellows.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/fellows_by_year.cgi?year=2024|title=2024 Class of Fellows of the AMS|publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=2023-11-08}}</ref> Elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Science]] in 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |title=National Academy of Sciences Elects Members and International Members - NAS |url=https://www.nasonline.org/news/2026-nas-election/ |access-date=May 6, 2026 |website=National Academy of Science |language=en-US|date=April 28, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Personal life==


In 2011, she married Daniel Panner, a viola player who teaches at [[Mannes School of Music]] and  [[Rutgers University]]. They have a son named Rafael.<ref>{{Cite news|title = Striking While the Iron Is Hot - NYTimes.com|url = http://mobile.nytimes.com/2014/01/12/realestate/striking-while-the-iron-is-hot.html|newspaper = The New York Times|access-date = 2016-02-03|date = 2014-01-08|last1 = Cohen|first1 = Joyce}}</ref>
